session.question: How does TSignal handle SPs, and what does it predict about their cleavage site and presence on benchmark datasets?
session.answer:
TSignal is a deep transformer-based neural network for signal peptide (SP) prediction. It combines BERT language models with dot-product attention to analyze protein sequences, enabling it to model both SP presence and cleavage-site location. (dumitrescu2023tsignalatransformer chunk 1)

For benchmark evaluation, TSignal predicts whether a protein contains an SP and the cleavage site separating the SP from the mature protein. On common benchmark datasets, it achieves competitive accuracy for SP presence prediction and state-of-the-art accuracy for cleavage-site prediction for most SP types and organism groups. (dumitrescu2023tsignalatransformer chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-8b3e7263: TSignal is a deep transformer-based neural network for signal peptide prediction. It combines BERT language models with dot-product attention to analyze protein sequences. The model predicts two things: whether a signal peptide is present in a protein and the cleavage site between the signal peptide and the mature protein. On common benchmark datasets, it achieves competitive accuracy for signal peptide presence prediction and state-of-the-art accuracy for cleavage-site prediction for most signal peptide types and organism groups.
From Alexandru Dumitrescu, Emmi Jokinen, Anja Paatero, Juho Kellosalo, Ville O Paavilainen, and Harri Lähdesmäki. Tsignal: a transformer model for signal peptide prediction. Bioinformatics, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btad228, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btad228.

pqac-41729a60: The paper introduces TSignal, a deep transformer-based model for signal peptide (SP) prediction. It uses BERT language models and dot-product attention to predict both the presence of signal peptides and the cleavage site between the SP and the mature protein. The abstract states that the authors evaluated TSignal on common benchmark datasets and found competitive accuracy for SP presence prediction and state-of-the-art cleavage site prediction for most SP types and organism groups. The work emphasizes that signal peptides are difficult to predict because they vary in length and lack conserved motifs.
From Alexandru Dumitrescu, Emmi Jokinen, Anja Paatero, Juho Kellosalo, Ville O Paavilainen, and Harri Lähdesmäki. Tsignal: a transformer model for signal peptide prediction. Bioinformatics, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btad228, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btad228.
